correctness.rationale: At Q_h=(0,h)x(0,1), vertical chords show r<=1. Every chord of length <1 must join adjacent sides because opposite-side chords have length >=1. Minimizing u²+v² for x/u+y/v=1 yields (x^(2/3)+y^(2/3))^3 and intercepts u=(x^(2/3)+y^(2/3))x^(1/3), v=...y^(1/3); if the minimum is <1, the intercepts fit the rectangle. The four-corner criterion, reflection, cutoff a, and integral follow. Substituting x=cos³t yields H(t)=3∫_0^t sin⁴s cos²s ds. Differentiating A and comparing a strictly increasing integrand proves (A/h)′>0; H~3t^5/5 and t~sqrt((2−h)/3) give the stated 4/(15sqrt3) coefficient and C² but not C³ regularity. Fresh independently written SciPy quadrature at h=1,1.25,1.5,1.9,1.99,2,2.1,3,20 agrees with H-formula within 3.3e−12, and ε=.1,.01,.001 scaled cusp quotients converge to 0.1539600718. These checks do not prove the infinite claim; the analytic reasoning does.
residual_risks: The self-supplied angular-grid and Monte Carlo experiment are bounded corroboration only; not used as proof.
